entities.name: University of Oxford
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The University of Oxford is the oldest English-speaking university in the world, with teaching dating from 1096 CE and developing rapidly after 1167 CE. A collegiate university of 44 colleges and 7 permanent private halls, Oxford has educated 28 British prime ministers, over 50 Nobel laureates, and shaped the English-speaking world's legal, political, and cultural tradition more than any other institution.

Oxford's origins lie in the royal court scholars gathered in Oxford's strategic location at the confluence of the Thames and Cherwell rivers. The expulsion of English students from Paris in 1167 CE accelerated Oxford's growth. By 1209 CE, violence between town and gown sent a group of scholars to Cambridge, founding that rival university. The collegiate system — individual colleges as self-governing scholarly communities within a larger university — was Oxford's unique innovation, creating communities that combined residence, dining, teaching, and scholarship.

Oxford's tutorial system, in which undergraduates meet one-on-one or in pairs with expert tutors weekly, is its most distinctive educational feature, producing extraordinary depth of individual scholarly development. Alumni include Roger Bacon (early scientific method), John Wycliffe (Bible translation), John Locke (social contract theory), Adam Smith (economics), Oscar Wilde (literature), Margaret Thatcher (chemistry to politics), and Bill Clinton. The Bodleian Library, one of Europe's oldest libraries (1602), holds over 13 million items including the Gutenberg Bible and Shakespeare First Folio.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Oxford University's 930-year history as the intellectual home of 28 British prime ministers, 70+ Nobel laureates, and foundational thinkers from Locke to Smith to Wilde makes it the single most consequential educational institution in the formation of English-speaking civilization. Its collegiate model and tutorial system have been replicated worldwide, and it directly spawned Cambridge in 1209.
